briefFull: The scheme aims to encourage large cardamom growers to adopt Improved Cardamom Curing Devices (ICCD) for drying cardamom, thereby improving the quality of the produce and enhancing its suitability for export.
details: The Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research & Development of Cardamom: Post-Harvest Improvement – Improved Cardamom Curing Devices (ICCD) for Large Cardamom in the North Eastern Region, Kalimpong, and Darjeeling Districts is implemented by the Spices Board India under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India. The scheme aims to encourage large cardamom growers to adopt Improved Cardamom Curing Devices (ICCD) for drying cardamom, thereby improving the quality of the produce and enhancing its suitability for export. The scheme is being implemented in accordance with the modalities and guidelines approved by the Competent Authority under the Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research & Development of Cardamom during the 15th Finance Commission period (2021–22 to 2025–26).
benefits:
- 75% subject to maximum of  ₹ 3,75,000 per unit for NE/SC/ST & Kalimpong and Darjeeling District of West Bengal & 90% Spice Producer's Groups in Identified Clusters subject to maximum of  ₹ 4,50,000/-.
- The assistance includes cost of transportation from South India since fabricators are not available elsewhere Large cardamom growers having a land holding size of 0.40 ha to 8 ha Assistance for groups/FPOs will be as in QGBG.
eligibility:
1.Sikkim, Darjeeling & Kalimpong district of West Bengal & other NE States
2. Designated Officials will conduct final inspection and recommend the eligible cases.
howToApply:
[Online]
**Registration**
Step 1: The applicant should visit the [ServicesPlus](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/) website.
Step 2: Click on the “[Register” ](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/citizenRegistration.html)option on the homepage.
Step 3: Fill out the registration form by entering Full Name, Email ID, Mobile Number, Password, selecting State, and Captcha.
Step 4: Review all details carefully and submit the registration form.
Step 5: An OTP will be sent to your registered mobile number or email; enter the OTP and click “Verify.”
Step 6: Registration will be completed successfully, and a confirmation message will be displayed or sent via email.
**Login**
Step 1: The applicant should visit the ServicesPlus website and click on [“Login.”](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/loginWindow.do)
Step 2: Enter your Email ID, Password, and Captcha.
Step 3: Select the relevant service/scheme name.
Step 4: Fill in the required details in the application form.
Step 5: Submit the application.

faqs.q: What is the ICCD for Large Cardamom scheme?
faqs.a: The scheme provides financial assistance to large cardamom growers for adopting Improved Cardamom Curing Devices (ICCD) to improve the quality of dried cardamom and promote exports.
The scheme is implemented by the Spices Board India under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India.

faqs.q: What is the objective of the scheme?
faqs.a: The objective is to encourage growers to use improved curing technology for drying large cardamom, resulting in better quality produce suitable for export markets.

faqs.q: Who is eligible to apply for assistance under the scheme?
faqs.a: Registered large cardamom growers with a landholding size between 0.40 hectares and 8 hectares are eligible to apply.

faqs.q: In which areas is the scheme available?
faqs.a: The scheme is available in Sikkim, Darjeeling and Kalimpong districts of West Bengal, and other North Eastern States.

faqs.q: What financial assistance is available for individual beneficiaries?
faqs.a: Eligible beneficiaries can receive 75% of the unit cost, subject to a maximum assistance of ₹3,75,000 per unit.

faqs.q: What assistance is available for SC/ST beneficiaries?
faqs.a: SC/ST beneficiaries are eligible for 75% of the unit cost, subject to a maximum assistance of ₹3,75,000 per unit.

faqs.q: What assistance is available for Spice Producer Groups in identified clusters?
faqs.a: Spice Producer Groups in identified clusters can receive 90% of the unit cost, subject to a maximum assistance of ₹4,50,000 per unit.

faqs.q: Does the assistance cover transportation costs?
faqs.a: Yes. The assistance includes transportation costs from South India, as approved fabricators are generally not available in the project area.

faqs.q: Is it mandatory to obtain a quotation from an approved manufacturer?
faqs.a: Yes. A quotation showing the capacity and cost of the curing device from an approved manufacturer or fabricator is mandatory.
